image.credit: Digitized Sky Survey 2 (STScI/NASA; Palomar Observatory and UK Schmidt Telescope), colored by CDS. Archival photographic plates in blue and red light. Cutout centered on the nebula, north up, 600 × 600; background lifted with an arcsinh stretch to show faint nebulosity.

source.title: CDS and ESA: DSS colored survey

sections.title: Two stars almost touching
sections.text: Pi Scorpii looks like one third-magnitude star, but its main component is a pair of hot blue stars only about 15 times the Sun’s radius apart, circling every 1.57 days. Their mutual distortion makes the system vary by 0.03 magnitudes. A faint third star orbits much farther out.

sh-2-9.name: Sh 2-9
sh-2-9.introduction: is a large cloud of gas and dust about 700 light-years away in Scorpius, around the multiple star Sigma Scorpii. It both glows red and reflects blue light. It lies only 2 degrees from Antares and 1 degree from the globular cluster Messier 4. It is also known as Gum 65.

image.alt: Bright Sigma Scorpii inside a blue haze and a large arc of pink ionized gas.
image.caption: Adam Block/Steward Observatory/University of Arizona · visible light
image.credit: Adam Block/Steward Observatory/University of Arizona. Visible light. Resized to 600 × 596 and converted to AVIF; colors unchanged.

sections.title: Beside the scorpion’s heart
sections.text: Sigma Scorpii’s official name, Alniyat, comes from the Arabic for “the arteries”, because it and Tau Scorpii flank Antares, the heart of the scorpion. Its brightest star is a blue giant with about 18 times the Sun’s mass, in a tight 33-day orbit with a companion.

ic-63.name: IC 63
ic-63.introduction: is the Ghost Nebula, a pale column of gas about 550 light-years away in Cassiopeia that is being slowly destroyed by its neighbor. Gamma Cassiopeiae both lights it and tears it apart from only 7.5 light-years away. It is also known as the Ghost of Cassiopeia.

image.alt: A pale, veiled column of gas with a bright upper edge, like a hooded ghost rising through red stars.
image.caption: ESA/Hubble, NASA · Hubble, hydrogen-alpha and visible light · released 2018
image.credit: ESA/Hubble, NASA. Hubble, hydrogen-alpha and visible light, released 2018. Resized to 600 × 609 and converted to AVIF; colors unchanged.

sections.title: A ghost with half a million years left
sections.text: Max Wolf discovered IC 63 on December 30, 1893, the same night as its neighbor IC 59. The star’s ultraviolet light makes its hydrogen glow red and sculpts its gas, with no sign that it is triggering new stars. The whole structure is moving apart and will probably be gone within half a million years.

sections.title: The first star with emission lines
sections.text: In 1866 Angelo Secchi observed Gamma Cassiopeiae and found the first stellar emission lines ever seen. The star spins so fast that it flings off a disk of hot gas. Apollo astronauts knew it as “Navi”, a name given in honor of Gus Grissom, whose middle name Ivan it spells backward.

running-man-nebula.name: Running Man Nebula
running-man-nebula.introduction: is a group of blue reflection nebulae about 1,290 light-years away, just north of the Orion Nebula at the top of Orion’s sword. Dark dust lanes trace the shape of a running figure, which shows up far better in photographs than through a telescope. It includes NGC 1973, NGC 1975 and NGC 1977.

image.alt: Blue and pink clouds around bright stars, with a dark figure outlined as if running.
image.caption: Adam Block/Mount Lemmon SkyCenter/University of Arizona · visible light · 2015
image.credit: Adam Block/Mount Lemmon SkyCenter/University of Arizona. Visible light, 2015. Resized to 600 × 599 and converted to AVIF; colors unchanged.

source.title: Wikimedia Commons: NGC 1977 Running Man Nebula

sections.title: Herschel’s two exclamation marks
sections.text: William Herschel discovered the brightest part in 1786 and wrote in his notes “!! 42 Orionis and neb”. Heinrich d’Arrest found the two smaller nebulae in 1862 and 1864. Today, 42 Orionis, a multiple star, is known to light up most of the reflecting dust.

sections.title: Young disks under attack
sections.text: In 2016 astronomers found seven evaporating disks around young stars in NGC 1977. All lie within 0.3 parsec of 42 Orionis and point toward it, as the star’s ultraviolet light and wind blow their gas into comet-like tails. It was the first time a B-type star was caught doing what O-type stars do in the Orion Nebula next door.

messier-78.name: Messier 78
messier-78.introduction: is the brightest diffuse reflection nebula in its group, about 1,320 light-years away in Orion, and it can be seen as a hazy patch in small telescopes. Two young B-type stars light it. Amateurs call it Casper the Friendly Ghost Nebula. It is also known as NGC 2068.

image.alt: Blue reflection nebulae cut by dark, twisting lanes of dust, with reddish gas in the background.
image.caption: ESO/Igor Chekalin · visible and near-infrared light · released 2011
image.credit: ESO/Igor Chekalin. Visible and near-infrared light, released 2011. Resized to 600 × 581 and converted to AVIF; colors unchanged.

source.title: ESO: Messier 78, a reflection nebula in Orion

sections.title: A comet-hunter’s catch
sections.text: Pierre Méchain discovered the nebula in 1780, and Charles Messier added it to his catalog of comet-like objects that same year. In a small telescope it still looks like a hazy patch, the sort of thing a comet hunter wanted to rule out.

sections.title: Hundreds of thousands of new objects
sections.text: Dust hides most of what lies in the cloud, but infrared observations reveal an embedded cluster, with 45 T Tauri stars and 17 Herbig–Haro jets. On May 23, 2024, the European Space Agency released a Euclid image of the region that shows hundreds of thousands of previously unseen objects, including substellar bodies.

ngc-2071.name: NGC 2071
ngc-2071.introduction: is a reflection nebula about 1,320 light-years away in Orion, just north of Messier 78 in the same Orion B cloud. William Herschel discovered it on January 1, 1784. The star HD 290861 at its center lights the dust, and Herbig–Haro objects nearby mark jets from stars still forming.

image.alt: A cream-colored cloud around a young star, with jets and dark dust, seen in near-infrared light.
image.caption: ESA/Euclid/Euclid Consortium/NASA/ERO2024 & Melina Thévenot · near-infrared · 2025
image.credit: ESA/Euclid/Euclid Consortium/NASA/ERO2024 & Melina Thévenot. Near-infrared, 2025. Resized to 600 × 388 and converted to AVIF; colors unchanged.

ngc-2023.name: NGC 2023
ngc-2023.introduction: is a large reflection nebula about 1,300 light-years away in Orion, on the edge of the Orion B cloud and only a short way north-east of the Horsehead. William Herschel discovered it on January 6, 1785. It is lit by the young star HD 37903.

image.alt: A bright blue star surrounded by a soft blue cloud, with faint rays and dust around it.
image.caption: KPNO/NOIRLab/NSF/AURA/Adam Block · visible light
image.credit: KPNO/NOIRLab/NSF/AURA/Adam Block. Visible light. Resized to 600 × 405 and converted to AVIF; colors unchanged.

sections.title: Carbon cages in space
sections.text: In 2007, spectra from the Spitzer Space Telescope showed emission from C60 fullerenes in this nebula and in the Iris Nebula. These molecules, made of 60 carbon atoms arranged in a closed cage, had never before been firmly detected as neutral molecules in interstellar space. They are among the largest molecules found there.

witch-head-nebula.name: Witch Head Nebula
witch-head-nebula.introduction: is a faint blue cloud about 3 degrees long and about 860 light-years away in Eridanus, shaped like the profile of a witch. It is lit by Rigel, the supergiant in Orion’s foot, about 2.5 degrees away in the sky. It is also known as IC 2118.

image.alt: A faint blue cloud in the shape of a witch’s profile near brilliant Rigel.
image.caption: Zdeněk Bardon/ESO · visible light
image.credit: Zdeněk Bardon/ESO. Visible light. Resized to 600 × 404 and converted to AVIF; colors unchanged.

sections.title: Why the witch is blue
sections.text: The dust grains in IC 2118 scatter blue light much better than red. Rigel’s light is already blue-white, so what reaches us looks strongly blue.

sections.title: A wind-blown star factory
sections.text: Radio observations show carbon monoxide throughout parts of the cloud, a sign of molecular gas and star formation, and young T Tauri stars have been found deep inside. The clouds lie near the outer edge of the vast Orion–Eridanus superbubble. Their comet-like heads point north-east, toward the massive stars of Orion OB1 that blew the bubble.

ngc-1333.name: NGC 1333
ngc-1333.introduction: is a reflection nebula about 940 light-years away in Perseus, around one of the most active nearby clusters of newborn stars. Most of the stars are about a million years old and still buried in their cloud. Eduard Schönfeld discovered it in 1855. It is also known as the Embryo Nebula.

image.alt: Blue reflection nebula around a bright star, dark dust at center and small red patches at right.
image.caption: KPNO/NOIRLab/NSF/AURA/Jay Lavine and Ali Huang/Adam Block · visible light · 2014
image.credit: KPNO/NOIRLab/NSF/AURA/Jay Lavine and Ali Huang/Adam Block. Visible light, 2014. Resized to 600 × 403 and converted to AVIF; colors unchanged.

sections.title: Worlds without suns
sections.text: Astronomers have found objects here with only a few times the mass of Jupiter, drifting free of any star. One, NN5, has about 5 Jupiter masses and may have a disk of its own. A 2024 Webb survey found no object below 4 Jupiter masses, despite being sensitive enough to detect them, which may mark the lower limit for star formation.

sections.title: A crowded nursery
sections.text: The region holds about 450 solar masses of gas and a cluster of around 150 stars. Twenty young stars are blasting out jets and outflows, and 95 X-ray sources belong to its embedded clusters. It is one of the best-studied objects of its type.

ic-348.name: IC 348
ic-348.introduction: is a star-forming region about 1,060 light-years away in Perseus, just south of Omicron Persei, where nebulosity surrounds a young cluster of about 400 stars. Webb has found its smallest free-floating objects here, with only 3–4 times the mass of Jupiter.

image.alt: Pink wisps of gas curving around bright young stars with diffraction spikes, in infrared light.
image.caption: NASA, ESA, CSA, STScI, K. Luhman (Penn State University) and C. Alves de Oliveira (ESA) · Webb NIRCam, near-infrared · released 2023
image.credit: NASA, ESA, CSA, STScI, K. Luhman (Penn State University) and C. Alves de Oliveira (ESA). Webb NIRCam, near-infrared, released 2023. Cropped, Resized to 600 × 603 and converted to AVIF; colors unchanged.

source.title: Wikimedia Commons: Star Cluster IC 348 (NIRCam image)

sections.title: Below the brown dwarfs
sections.text: Webb has since found objects in this cluster down to about 2 Jupiter masses, far below what stars normally reach. The faintest show a chemical signature that does not fit any known class, leading researchers to propose a new spectral type, “H”.

sections.title: The amino acid that wasn’t
sections.text: In 2023, researchers claimed to have detected tryptophan, an amino acid, in the gas of IC 348. It would have been a striking find, but a re-analysis of the Spitzer data found none. Webb observations and an improved laboratory spectrum then confirmed its absence, and the supposed lines turned out to be instrumental artifacts.

ic-59.name: IC 59
ic-59.introduction: is a faint, mostly reflecting cloud about 550 light-years away in Cassiopeia, the quieter sibling of the Ghost Nebula, IC 63. Both are sculpted by Gamma Cassiopeiae, but IC 59 lies in front of the star and has no sharp front of ionized gas. It is also known as LBN 620.

image.alt: A faint blue wedge of nebula with a thin red edge among many stars.
image.caption: Adam Block/Mount Lemmon SkyCenter/University of Arizona · visible light · 2010
image.credit: Adam Block/Mount Lemmon SkyCenter/University of Arizona. Visible light, 2010. Cropped, Resized to 600 × 750 and converted to AVIF; colors unchanged.

sections.title: The sibling on the near side
sections.text: Max Wolf discovered IC 59 on December 30, 1893, the same night as IC 63. Its closest tip lies about 13.5 light-years from the star. Together the two are the closest photodissociation regions to the Sun, places where starlight breaks molecules apart, and they look different because of their different distances from the star.

iris-nebula.name: Iris Nebula
iris-nebula.introduction: is a bright, flower-like reflection nebula about 1,160 light-years away in Cepheus, lit by the young star HD 200775. Together with NGC 2023, it was the first place where neutral C60 molecules were firmly identified in interstellar space. William Herschel discovered it in 1794. It is also known as NGC 7023 and Caldwell 4.

image.alt: Blue, petal-like clouds spreading around a bright central star, with dark dust at the edges.
image.caption: T.A. Rector (University of Alaska Anchorage) and H. Schweiker (WIYN and NOIRLab/NSF/AURA) · visible light and hydrogen-alpha · 2009
image.credit: T.A. Rector (University of Alaska Anchorage) and H. Schweiker (WIYN and NOIRLab/NSF/AURA). Visible light and hydrogen-alpha, 2009. Resized to 600 × 551 and converted to AVIF; colors unchanged.

sections.title: How to build a carbon cage
sections.text: C60 was thought to form in the hot, dense envelopes of evolved stars, yet here it appears in a thin, cold cloud under strong ultraviolet light. Models suggest that large carbon molecules lose their hydrogen, fold into a floppy cage and shrink until they reach C60. HD 200775 supplies the light.

sections.title: A cavity carved by two stars
sections.text: At the center is a pair of young Herbig Ae/Be stars. Their outflows have carved a two-lobed cavity in a nebula about 6 light-years across. Where the cavity walls meet starlight, bright ridges of glowing gas mark the zones in which molecules are being broken apart.

helix-nebula.name: Helix Nebula
helix-nebula.introduction: is one of the closest bright planetary nebulae, about 650 light-years away in Aquarius: the gas shed by a dying Sun-like star, around its hot core. Its striking shape has earned it the nicknames “Eye of God” and “Eye of Sauron”. It is also known as NGC 7293 and Caldwell 63.

image.alt: A vast eye-shaped ring, blue-green inside and orange-red outside, around a faint central star.
image.caption: ESO · Wide Field Imager, visible light · released 2009
image.credit: ESO. Wide Field Imager, visible light, released 2009. Resized to 600 × 555 and converted to AVIF; colors unchanged.

sections.title: Forty thousand cometary knots
sections.text: The Helix was the first planetary nebula found to contain cometary knots, and it holds about 40,000 of them. Each has a dense core of molecular gas about the size of the Solar System, a bright cusp facing the central star and a tail pointing away.

sections.title: A star eating its past
sections.text: The central white dwarf has a temperature of 120,000 K and a radius of only 17,000 km. Its infrared glow reveals a ring of dust 30–100 au wide, possibly fed by thousands of comets. A 2025 X-ray study suggests the star may be accreting the remains of a Jupiter-like planet.

sections.title: A flattened edge
sections.text: The whole structure is about 2.5 light-years across and has been expanding for roughly 10,000 years. Its outermost ring looks flattened on one side, where it is running into the surrounding interstellar medium.

dumbbell-nebula.name: Dumbbell Nebula
dumbbell-nebula.introduction: was the first planetary nebula ever discovered, by Charles Messier in 1764. About 1,270 light-years away in Vulpecula and bright enough to see in binoculars, it is a popular target for amateur telescopes. It is also known as Messier 27 and NGC 6853.

image.alt: A blue-green hourglass-shaped cloud inside a fainter red-tinted oval, on a dense star field.
image.caption: REU program/NOIRLab/NSF/AURA · approximately true color
image.credit: REU program/NOIRLab/NSF/AURA. Approximately true color. Resized to 600 × 514 and converted to AVIF; colors unchanged.

sections.title: A young nebula
sections.text: Its gas expands at about 31 km/s, which gives the nebula an age of around 9,800 years, consistent with the 14,600-year upper limit from its measured growth on the sky. From our viewpoint we see a stretched spheroid from the side, along its equator, which is what gives it the shape of a dumbbell.

sections.title: Dark knots in the glow
sections.text: The central region is marked by dark and bright knots with cusped heads and dark tails, much like those of the Helix Nebula. The bright cusps are places where the central star’s light strikes dense clumps of gas. That star, at about 0.055 times the Sun’s radius, is larger than most known white dwarfs.

ngc-1360.name: NGC 1360
ngc-1360.introduction: is a large planetary nebula about 1,290 light-years away in Fornax, known as the Comet Planetary Nebula or the Robin’s Egg Nebula for its smooth, blue-green glow. Friedrich Winnecke discovered it in January 1868.

image.alt: A smooth turquoise oval cloud with a small star at its center.
image.caption: Adam Block/Mount Lemmon SkyCenter/University of Arizona · visible light · 2014
image.credit: Adam Block/Mount Lemmon SkyCenter/University of Arizona. Visible light, 2014. Resized to 600 × 643 and converted to AVIF; colors unchanged.

sections.title: A partner confirmed after 40 years
sections.text: The central star was suspected of being double as early as 1977, but only in 2017 was that confirmed. It consists of a low-mass O-type star of 0.555 solar masses and a white dwarf of 0.679 solar masses.

medusa-nebula.name: Medusa Nebula
medusa-nebula.introduction: is an old, faint planetary nebula about 1,930 light-years away in Gemini, whose curling filaments recall the snake hair of the mythical Medusa. It is also known as Abell 21 and Sh 2-274.

image.alt: Twisting red, orange and blue filaments of gas like strands of hair.
image.caption: ESO · VLT FORS, visible light · released 2015
image.credit: ESO. VLT FORS, visible light, released 2015. Resized to 600 × 625 and converted to AVIF; colors unchanged.

source.title: ESO: The VLT images the Medusa Nebula

sections.title: Slow to be recognized
sections.text: George Abell, of UCLA, discovered it in 1955 and classified it as an old planetary nebula. Because it is so large, its light is spread very thin, and it took until 1971 for Soviet astronomers, using its expansion speed and radio emission, to conclude that this was most likely right. Its central star is of the PG 1159 type.

sections.title: The Sun’s future
sections.text: The Medusa formed when a dying star shed its outer layers into space. In 2015, ESO’s Very Large Telescope took the most detailed image of the nebula so far, showing what the Sun will eventually become.

source.title: ESO: The VLT images the Medusa Nebula

abell-31.name: Abell 31
abell-31.introduction: is one of the largest known planetary nebulae, an ancient shell about 1,770 light-years away in Cancer and some 7 parsecs (about 23 light-years) across. One side is brighter than the rest because it is running into the interstellar gas around it. It is also known as Sh 2-290.

image.alt: A huge round shell, pale blue inside and fringed by rippling red filaments.
image.caption: T.A. Rector (University of Alaska Anchorage) and H. Schweiker (WIYN and NOIRLab/NSF/AURA) · hydrogen-alpha, sulfur and oxygen filters
image.credit: T.A. Rector (University of Alaska Anchorage) and H. Schweiker (WIYN and NOIRLab/NSF/AURA). Hydrogen-alpha, sulfur and oxygen filters. Resized to 600 × 618 and converted to AVIF; colors unchanged.

sections.title: Blue inside, red outside
sections.text: Oxygen fills the center of the nebula with blue light, while hydrogen forms a red ring at its edge. The nebula is now so old and dim that its gas is dispersing into the interstellar medium. At the center lies a white dwarf of spectral type DAO.

abell-7.name: Abell 7
abell-7.introduction: is a faint, nearly round planetary nebula about 1,690 light-years away in Lepus, about 8 light-years in diameter. Narrowband filters bring out complex detail in what otherwise looks like a smooth sphere. At its center is a hot, fading white dwarf.

image.alt: A small round violet shell with red patches in a sparse star field.
image.caption: Jerry Macon · hydrogen-alpha, oxygen and RGB filters · 2020
image.credit: Jerry Macon. Hydrogen-alpha, oxygen and RGB filters, 2020. Resized to 600 × 401 and converted to AVIF; colors unchanged.

abell-36.name: Abell 36
abell-36.introduction: is a faint planetary nebula about 1,360 light-years away in Virgo, surrounding a dying Sun-like star. George Abell discovered it in 1955. It is also known as ESO 577-24.

image.alt: A bubble of pink and blue glowing gas with a bright central star and dark gaps.
image.caption: ESO · VLT FORS2, visible light · released 2019
image.credit: ESO. VLT FORS2, visible light, released 2019. Resized to 600 × 653 and converted to AVIF; colors unchanged.

source.title: ESO: A fleeting moment in time

sections.title: A blink of an eye
sections.text: A planetary nebula like this one lasts only about 10,000 years, an instant in astronomical terms. As the shell of glowing gas expands and grows dimmer, it will slowly disappear from sight, leaving the star’s simmering core behind.

source.title: ESO: A fleeting moment in time

puwe-1.name: PuWe 1
puwe-1.introduction: is a very faint planetary nebula about 1,290 light-years away in Lynx, next to the border with Camelopardalis. The Austrian astronomers Alois Purgathofer and Ronald Weinberger discovered it in 1980.

image.alt: A round shell, pale blue inside with a bright red and orange rim on one side.
image.caption: T.A. Rector (University of Alaska Anchorage) and H. Schweiker (WIYN and NOIRLab/NSF/AURA) · hydrogen-alpha and oxygen filters
image.credit: T.A. Rector (University of Alaska Anchorage) and H. Schweiker (WIYN and NOIRLab/NSF/AURA). Hydrogen-alpha and oxygen filters. Resized to 600 × 546 and converted to AVIF; colors unchanged.

sections.title: Fading as it grows
sections.text: PuWe 1 is one of the largest and faintest planetary nebulae known. It formed when a red giant blew off its outer layers. A planetary nebula gets fainter as it expands, because its gas moves ever farther from the white dwarf that energizes it, and this one has spread very thin.

vdb-1.name: vdB 1
vdb-1.introduction: is a small, bright blue reflection nebula about 1,310 light-years away in Cassiopeia, a few arcminutes south-east of Caph, whose glare makes it hard to observe. It is the first entry in Sidney van den Bergh’s 1966 catalog. The star HD 627 lights it.

image.alt: Three bright stars inside a soft blue cloud in a rich star field.
image.caption: Adam Block/Mount Lemmon SkyCenter/University of Arizona · visible light · 2012
image.credit: Adam Block/Mount Lemmon SkyCenter/University of Arizona. Visible light, 2012. Resized to 600 × 449 and converted to AVIF; colors unchanged.

sections.title: A young star with a hidden twin
sections.text: Inside the cloud is V633 Cassiopeiae, a young star identified in 1960 that shows strong flares. In the 1990s astronomers found a companion deep in the cloud that produces most of the region’s near-infrared light. Several jets stream from this area, one of them about 7 light-years long and visible even in optical light.

vdb-4.name: vdB 4
vdb-4.introduction: is a faint blue reflection nebula about 1,820 light-years away in Cassiopeia, on the north-west side of the open cluster NGC 225. It is lit by the young emission-line star BD+61 154 and forms the illuminated part of a dark cloud called LDN 1297.

image.alt: A bright star in a blue cloud with dark fingers of dust, under the stars of NGC 225.
image.caption: Adam Block/Mount Lemmon SkyCenter/University of Arizona · visible light · 2012
image.credit: Adam Block/Mount Lemmon SkyCenter/University of Arizona. Visible light, 2012. Resized to 600 × 398 and converted to AVIF; colors unchanged.

sections.title: Is the cluster next door really related?
sections.text: Astronomers disagree about NGC 225. One earlier study found that the nebula and its young stars have nothing to do with the cluster, which it dated to about 120 million years. A 2006 study found young stars in the cluster and argued for a direct link, which would make it younger than 10 million years.

vdb-9.name: vdB 9
vdb-9.introduction: is a faint blue reflection nebula about 1,510 light-years away in Cassiopeia, near SU Cassiopeiae, one of the few Cepheid variables that light a nebula. A long lane of dark dust runs to its south-west, visible even in a telescope as a band with few background stars.

image.alt: Bright SU Cassiopeiae in a glowing halo, with a dark lane of dust at left and a pale streak below.
image.caption: Digitized Sky Survey 2 · STScI/NASA, colored by CDS · visible-light survey composite · contrast stretched
image.credit: Digitized Sky Survey 2 (STScI/NASA; Palomar Observatory and UK Schmidt Telescope), colored by CDS. Archival photographic plates in blue and red light. Cutout centered on the nebula, north up, 600 × 600; background lifted with an arcsinh stretch to show faint nebulosity.

source.title: CDS and ESA: DSS colored survey

vdb-16.name: vdB 16
vdb-16.introduction: is a bluish reflection nebula about 950 light-years away, in Aries at the outer end of the Perseus cloud. It is lit by a ninth-magnitude F-type star. About a degree to the north lies the dark cloud Barnard 204, and young stars across the region show that stars are still forming here.

image.alt: Two bright stars with faint blue arcs of nebulosity around them.
image.caption: Digitized Sky Survey 2 · STScI/NASA, colored by CDS · visible-light survey composite
image.credit: Digitized Sky Survey 2 (STScI/NASA; Palomar Observatory and UK Schmidt Telescope), colored by CDS. Archival photographic plates in blue and red light. Cutout centered on the nebula, north up, 600 × 600.

source.title: CDS and ESA: DSS colored survey

vdb-18.name: vdB 18
vdb-18.introduction: is a faint blue reflection nebula about 1,020 light-years away in Perseus, halfway between Algol and Xi Persei. The star that lights it, V496 Persei, is a chemically peculiar variable. Beyond the northern edge of the Perseus cloud, this nebula connects to dark clouds reaching toward the California Nebula.

image.alt: A bright blue star in a small blue haze, with thin grey filaments below.
image.caption: Digitized Sky Survey 2 · STScI/NASA, colored by CDS · visible-light survey composite · contrast stretched
image.credit: Digitized Sky Survey 2 (STScI/NASA; Palomar Observatory and UK Schmidt Telescope), colored by CDS. Archival photographic plates in blue and red light. Cutout centered on the nebula, north up, 600 × 600; background lifted with an arcsinh stretch to show faint nebulosity.

source.title: CDS and ESA: DSS colored survey

vdb-24.name: vdB 24
vdb-24.introduction: is a reflection nebula about 1,390 light-years away in Perseus, embedded in a large dark cloud about a degree south-west of Epsilon Persei. Its light comes from XY Persei, a massive young Herbig Ae/Be star, which has a companion about 500 au away.

image.alt: Blue and pale nebulosity near XY Persei, embedded in a deep orange-brown dust cloud.
image.caption: T.A. Rector (University of Alaska Anchorage) and H. Schweiker (WIYN and NOIRLab/NSF/AURA) · visible light
image.credit: T.A. Rector (University of Alaska Anchorage) and H. Schweiker (WIYN and NOIRLab/NSF/AURA). Visible light. Resized to 600 × 482 and converted to AVIF; colors unchanged.

sections.title: Three pieces of blue
sections.text: The lit part of the cloud is not uniform. It splits into three sections: one in the north-west, touching other dark regions; a brighter, elongated one in the south-west; and the brightest of all, just south of the star.

vdb-29.name: vdB 29
vdb-29.introduction: is a blue reflection nebula about 510 light-years away, on the border between Taurus and Auriga, lit by the seventh-magnitude blue-white star HD 30378. The cloud stretches west of the star and fades into a small dark patch, close to the star-forming clouds of Taurus.

image.alt: A blue star at the edge of a broad, pale blue cloud.
image.caption: Digitized Sky Survey 2 · STScI/NASA, colored by CDS · visible-light survey composite · contrast stretched
image.credit: Digitized Sky Survey 2 (STScI/NASA; Palomar Observatory and UK Schmidt Telescope), colored by CDS. Archival photographic plates in blue and red light. Cutout centered on the nebula, north up, 600 × 600; background lifted with an arcsinh stretch to show faint nebulosity.

source.title: CDS and ESA: DSS colored survey

vdb-31.name: vdB 31
vdb-31.introduction: is a blue reflection nebula about 510 light-years away in Auriga, around AB Aurigae, a young star with a disk where a planet may be forming. It belongs to the young Taurus–Auriga association.

image.alt: A small blue nebula beside black dust knots, trailing into a long faint brown cloud.
image.caption: Nico Carver (Nebula Photos) · visible light · 2025
image.credit: Nico Carver (Nebula Photos). Visible light, 2025. Resized to 600 × 523 and converted to AVIF; colors unchanged.

sections.title: A planet caught forming
sections.text: ALMA images from 2017 show a dusty disk around AB Aurigae with a clear gap and gas spiraling through it. In April 2022 astronomers reported a planet-like clump 93 au from the star, called AB Aurigae b. It may be a forming planet in its own disk, or a part of the disk collapsing under its own gravity, a process reported in Nature in September 2024.

sections.title: Found on old plates
sections.text: Mary Doris Applegate Beach discovered that AB Aurigae varies by examining 150 photographic plates taken between 1914 and 1921. The star has about 2.4 times the mass of the Sun and shines with 38 times its light. An encounter with a dense cloudlet may have produced an additional nebula.

vdb-37.name: vdB 37
vdb-37.introduction: is a very red reflection nebula about 1,180 light-years away in Orion, lit by the red giant HD 34454, an M-type semi-regular variable also known as V1057 Orionis. Dust around a red star simply keeps its color.

image.alt: A red-orange star with a faint wisp of ruddy nebulosity around it.
image.caption: Digitized Sky Survey 2 · STScI/NASA, colored by CDS · visible-light survey composite
image.credit: Digitized Sky Survey 2 (STScI/NASA; Palomar Observatory and UK Schmidt Telescope), colored by CDS. Archival photographic plates in blue and red light. Cutout centered on the nebula, north up, 600 × 600.

source.title: CDS and ESA: DSS colored survey

vdb-38.name: vdB 38
vdb-38.introduction: is the soft blue glow around the star HD 34989, about 1,280 light-years away in Orion. It lies within the Raspberry Nebula, a much larger cloud that hides several kinds of nebula in one.

image.alt: Bright HD 34989 in a soft blue glow, inside a red bloom of gas above a dark blue dust edge.
image.caption: KPNO/NOIRLab/NSF/AURA/T.A. Rector (University of Alaska Anchorage/NOIRLab) · visible light and hydrogen-alpha · released 2023
image.credit: KPNO/NOIRLab/NSF/AURA/T.A. Rector (University of Alaska Anchorage/NOIRLab). Visible light and hydrogen-alpha, released 2023. Resized to 600 × 604 and converted to AVIF; colors unchanged.

sections.title: A raspberry built like an onion
sections.text: The red bloom of the Raspberry Nebula (LBN 867) is gas ionized by HD 34989. Around the star itself, vdB 38 is starlight reflecting off nearby dust. HD 34989 itself is about as bright as Uranus appears from Earth.

sections.title: The dark half of the cloud
sections.text: Part of the same cloud is not lit at all. Known as LDN 1588, or Barnard 223, it appears as a dark nebula that blocks the light of the stars behind it. All of this lies about 2 degrees from Bellatrix, on the outskirts of the Orion complex.

vdb-42.name: vdB 42
vdb-42.introduction: is a faint reflection nebula about 1,340 light-years away in Orion, lit by EY Orionis, an eclipsing binary that changes between the ninth and tenth magnitudes every 16.7 days. It belongs to the same complex of clouds as the Orion Nebula, in a region full of young stars and their jets.

image.alt: A white star at the lower edge of a pale, slanted patch of grey-blue nebulosity.
image.caption: ESO/Digitized Sky Survey 2; crop on Wikimedia Commons · survey composite
image.credit: ESO/Digitized Sky Survey 2; crop on Wikimedia Commons. Survey composite. Cropped, Resized to 528 × 660 and converted to AVIF; colors unchanged.

ic-420.name: IC 420
ic-420.introduction: is a faint, very blue reflection nebula about 1,350 light-years away in Orion, near the blue giant HD 36540. It lies in the same complex as the Running Man Nebula, and the star that lights it is a fast-spinning variable also known as V1101 Orionis.

image.alt: A bright double star at the edge of a pale blue-grey haze.
image.caption: Digitized Sky Survey 2 · STScI/NASA, colored by CDS · visible-light survey composite
image.credit: Digitized Sky Survey 2 (STScI/NASA; Palomar Observatory and UK Schmidt Telescope), colored by CDS. Archival photographic plates in blue and red light. Cutout centered on the nebula, north up, 600 × 600.

source.title: CDS and ESA: DSS colored survey

vdb-49.name: vdB 49
vdb-49.introduction: is a blue reflection nebula about 1,650 light-years away in Orion, lit by the fourth-magnitude star Omega Orionis. It sits close to the edge of Barnard’s Loop, the great arc of gas that encircles much of the constellation.

image.alt: The bright star Omega Orionis in a small round blue cloud.
image.caption: Digitized Sky Survey 2 · STScI/NASA, colored by CDS · visible-light survey composite
image.credit: Digitized Sky Survey 2 (STScI/NASA; Palomar Observatory and UK Schmidt Telescope), colored by CDS. Archival photographic plates in blue and red light. Cutout centered on the nebula, north up, 600 × 600.

source.title: CDS and ESA: DSS colored survey

sections.title: The first magnetic Be star
sections.text: Omega Orionis spins so fast that it is a Be star, with a rotation rate of up to 450 km/s. It was the first star of this class in which a magnetic field was measured, about 1,000 times as strong as Earth’s. It radiates about 6,000 times the light of the Sun.

vdb-50.name: vdB 50

source.title: Van den Bergh (1966): A study of reflection nebulae

vdb-50.introduction: is a very blue reflection nebula about 1,340 light-years away in the Orion B cloud, north-west of the Flame Nebula. It is lit by the star HD 37674.

image.alt: A blue-white star in a vertical blue haze, with a second bright star at upper right.
image.caption: Digitized Sky Survey 2 · STScI/NASA, colored by CDS · visible-light survey composite
image.credit: Digitized Sky Survey 2 (STScI/NASA; Palomar Observatory and UK Schmidt Telescope), colored by CDS. Archival photographic plates in blue and red light. Cutout centered on the nebula, north up, 600 × 600.

source.title: CDS and ESA: DSS colored survey

ic-432.name: IC 432
ic-432.introduction: is a very bright blue reflection nebula about 1,280 light-years away in Orion, about half a degree north of Alnitak and surrounded by many other nebulae. It is lit by V901 Orionis, a blue subgiant that varies between magnitudes 6.97 and 7.02 every 1.54 days. Behind it lies the dark cloud that holds the Flame and Horsehead Nebulae.

image.alt: A bright star inside an oval of blue, filamentary nebulosity.
image.caption: Digitized Sky Survey 2 · STScI/NASA, colored by CDS · visible-light survey composite
image.credit: Digitized Sky Survey 2 (STScI/NASA; Palomar Observatory and UK Schmidt Telescope), colored by CDS. Archival photographic plates in blue and red light. Cutout centered on the nebula, north up, 600 × 600.

source.title: CDS and ESA: DSS colored survey

ic-435.name: IC 435
ic-435.introduction: is a very bright blue reflection nebula about 1,230 light-years away in Orion, some 20 arcminutes east of NGC 2023 and north-east of the Horsehead. It is part of the same giant cloud, LDN 1630, and it is lit by the blue-white star HD 38087.

image.alt: A bright star in the middle of a compact, fan-like blue nebula.
image.caption: Digitized Sky Survey 2 · STScI/NASA, colored by CDS · visible-light survey composite
image.credit: Digitized Sky Survey 2 (STScI/NASA; Palomar Observatory and UK Schmidt Telescope), colored by CDS. Archival photographic plates in blue and red light. Cutout centered on the nebula, north up, 600 × 600.

source.title: CDS and ESA: DSS colored survey

sections.title: Unusually large grains
sections.text: The nebula is dense and splits into two regions with distinct surface brightness. Its dust grains are larger than the average seen in similar nebulae.

ic-1287.name: IC 1287
ic-1287.introduction: is an extended blue reflection nebula about 740 light-years away in Scutum, lying along the plane of the Milky Way near the small open cluster NGC 6649. It is lit by HD 170740, a B2 binary or multiple star of magnitude 5.7. Its central part is catalogued separately as vdB 124.

image.alt: A blue-white star at the center of a diamond-shaped blue cloud, with dark clouds around it.
image.caption: Digitized Sky Survey 2 · STScI/NASA, colored by CDS · visible-light survey composite · contrast stretched
image.credit: Digitized Sky Survey 2 (STScI/NASA; Palomar Observatory and UK Schmidt Telescope), colored by CDS. Archival photographic plates in blue and red light. Cutout centered on the nebula, north up, 600 × 600; background lifted with an arcsinh stretch to show faint nebulosity.

source.title: CDS and ESA: DSS colored survey

vdb-127.name: vdB 127
vdb-127.introduction: is a large, faint, reddish reflection nebula about 550 light-years away in Sagitta, roughly twice the width of the full Moon. It is catalogued near Delta Sagittae, a pair made of an M-type red giant and a B-type main-sequence star that orbit each other every 10 years. The IAU gave the star the name Zuoqi in June 2026.

vdb-134.name: vdB 134
vdb-134.introduction: is a faint blue reflection nebula about 1,280 light-years away in Cygnus, about 4 degrees from Deneb. It is lit by Omega-1 Cygni, a naked-eye blue subgiant that pulses very slightly, by 0.03 magnitudes every 1.137 days.

image.alt: The bright star Omega-1 Cygni in a soft blue glow among rich star fields.
image.caption: Digitized Sky Survey 2 · STScI/NASA, colored by CDS · visible-light survey composite · contrast stretched
image.credit: Digitized Sky Survey 2 (STScI/NASA; Palomar Observatory and UK Schmidt Telescope), colored by CDS. Archival photographic plates in blue and red light. Cutout centered on the nebula, north up, 600 × 600; background lifted with an arcsinh stretch to show faint nebulosity.

source.title: CDS and ESA: DSS colored survey

vdb-141.name: vdB 141
vdb-141.introduction: is the Ghost Nebula, a faint brown cloud with raised, ghostly arms about 1,110 light-years away in Cepheus, a little over a degree from the Iris Nebula. Its catalog name is simply its number in Sidney van den Bergh’s 1966 list of reflection nebulae. It is also known as Sh 2-136.

image.alt: Brown, ghostly dust shapes with raised arms, lit from within by a cream-colored glow.
image.caption: T.A. Rector (University of Alaska Anchorage) and H. Schweiker (WIYN and NOIRLab/NSF/AURA) · visible light · 2009
image.credit: T.A. Rector (University of Alaska Anchorage) and H. Schweiker (WIYN and NOIRLab/NSF/AURA). Visible light, 2009. Resized to 600 × 300 and converted to AVIF; colors unchanged.

sections.title: A brown glow from within
sections.text: Several stars embedded in this dust cloud light it from within, which gives it a yellow-brown color. The globule, catalogued as CB 230, is over 2 light-years across.

vdb-149.name: vdB 149
vdb-149.introduction: is a small, very blue reflection nebula about 1,120 light-years away in Cepheus, lit by BD+72 1018, a blue-white B8 star. The seventh-magnitude orange star just to the south, HD 210615, is a foreground bystander.

image.alt: A small blue-white star in a faint blue haze, with orange stars around it.
image.caption: Digitized Sky Survey 2 · STScI/NASA, colored by CDS · visible-light survey composite
image.credit: Digitized Sky Survey 2 (STScI/NASA; Palomar Observatory and UK Schmidt Telescope), colored by CDS. Archival photographic plates in blue and red light. Cutout centered on the nebula, north up, 600 × 600.

source.title: CDS and ESA: DSS colored survey

sections.title: Inside the cloud, or in front of it?
sections.text: The nebula appears to belong to the large dark cloud LDN 1235, like its neighbor vdB 150. Radial-velocity studies suggest that this is only perspective, and that vdB 149 lies in the same direction by chance. The star’s parallax, on the other hand, points to a distance similar to vdB 150’s.

vdb-150.name: vdB 150
vdb-150.introduction: is a very blue reflection nebula about 1,110 light-years away in Cepheus, roughly a third of the way from Alfirk to Alrai. It is a lit part of the dark cloud LDN 1235, shining under the B8 star HD 210806. The cloud’s cold dust also glows in infrared light.

image.alt: A bright star on a dark, broad band of dust with thin blue haze along it.
image.caption: Digitized Sky Survey 2 · STScI/NASA, colored by CDS · visible-light survey composite
image.credit: Digitized Sky Survey 2 (STScI/NASA; Palomar Observatory and UK Schmidt Telescope), colored by CDS. Archival photographic plates in blue and red light. Cutout centered on the nebula, north up, 600 × 600.

source.title: CDS and ESA: DSS colored survey

vdb-152.name: vdB 152
vdb-152.introduction: is a bright blue reflection nebula about 1,210 light-years away in Cepheus, sitting at the tip of a long, dark globule of dust known as Barnard 175. It is lit by the star BD+69 1231. Astronomers have found a jet from a newly forming star in the same structure, called HH 450.

image.alt: A bright pale nebula atop a long brown pillar of dust, with thin red filaments at the right edge.
image.caption: T.A. Rector (University of Alaska Anchorage) and H. Schweiker (WIYN and NOIRLab/NSF/AURA) · visible light and hydrogen-alpha
image.credit: T.A. Rector (University of Alaska Anchorage) and H. Schweiker (WIYN and NOIRLab/NSF/AURA). Visible light and hydrogen-alpha. Cropped, Resized to 600 × 584 and converted to AVIF; colors unchanged.

sections.title: A supernova remnant at the door
sections.text: Thin red filaments close to the nebula are the remains of a supernova explosion. It is not yet clear whether the expanding remnant will collide with vdB 152 and its dark cloud.

sh-2-68.name: Sh 2-68
sh-2-68.introduction: is an old, faint planetary nebula about 1,330 light-years away in Serpens, so diffuse that Stewart Sharpless listed it among H II regions. It has the largest proper motion ever measured for a planetary nebula. It is also known as the Flaming Skull Nebula.

image.alt: A broken blue bubble trailing a wide orange plume toward the upper right.
image.caption: T.A. Rector (University of Alaska Anchorage) and H. Schweiker (WIYN and NOIRLab/NSF/AURA) · hydrogen-alpha and oxygen filters
image.credit: T.A. Rector (University of Alaska Anchorage) and H. Schweiker (WIYN and NOIRLab/NSF/AURA). Hydrogen-alpha and oxygen filters. Resized to 600 × 452 and converted to AVIF; colors unchanged.

sections.title: A tail from moving through space
sections.text: Estimated to be 30,000–45,000 years old, the nebula is plowing through interstellar gas, which has stalled its expansion. The result is a long, diffuse tail streaming away from the bluish, oxygen-rich core. Its central star, the white dwarf WD 1822+008, now sits off-center in the nebula.

pfp-1.name: PFP 1

source.title: Pierce et al. (2004): PFP 1, a large planetary nebula caught in the first stages of ISM interaction

pfp-1.introduction: is one of the largest planetary nebulae of its type, about 1,740 light-years away in Monoceros and some 19 arcminutes across, about two-thirds of the width of the full Moon. Its surface is so faint that it evaded every survey until 2004.

sections.title: Found by accident
sections.text: Astronomers came across this nebula while working through images from the AAO/UKST H-alpha Survey. It forms a remarkably even ring, with near-perfect circular symmetry. Only its north-west edge breaks the pattern and shines brighter, the first sign that the shell has begun to run into the interstellar gas around it.

vdb-138.name: vdB 138
vdb-138.introduction: is a small, faint blue reflection nebula in Cygnus, roughly 1,960 light-years away, although the parallax of its star is uncertain. It is lit by HD 199714, a blue supergiant of magnitude 8.3.

image.alt: A bright star with a patch of blue nebulosity in a crowded Milky Way field.
image.caption: Digitized Sky Survey 2 · STScI/NASA, colored by CDS · visible-light survey composite · contrast stretched
image.credit: Digitized Sky Survey 2 (STScI/NASA; Palomar Observatory and UK Schmidt Telescope), colored by CDS. Archival photographic plates in blue and red light. Cutout centered on the nebula, north up, 600 × 600; background lifted with an arcsinh stretch to show faint nebulosity.

source.title: CDS and ESA: DSS colored survey

vdb-151.name: vdB 151
vdb-151.introduction: is a faint reflection nebula about 570 light-years away in Lacerta, near the fourth-magnitude orange giant HD 211073, itself one star in a binary system.

ced-184.name: Ced 184

source.title: Magakian (2003): Merged catalogue of reflection nebulae

ced-184.introduction: is a faint reflection nebula about 1,230 light-years away in Cepheus, around the blue-white star HD 198793. It is also known as LBN 422.

image.alt: A blue-white star in a broad blue haze in a dense star field.
image.caption: Digitized Sky Survey 2 · STScI/NASA, colored by CDS · visible-light survey composite · contrast stretched
image.credit: Digitized Sky Survey 2 (STScI/NASA; Palomar Observatory and UK Schmidt Telescope), colored by CDS. Archival photographic plates in blue and red light. Cutout centered on the nebula, north up, 600 × 600; background lifted with an arcsinh stretch to show faint nebulosity.

source.title: CDS and ESA: DSS colored survey

ic-4591.name: IC 4591
ic-4591.introduction: is a thin veil of reflecting dust about 480 light-years away in Scorpius, just south of the bright stars in the scorpion’s head. Its light comes from 13 Scorpii (also c2 Scorpii), a blue B2 star of magnitude 4.6 that is easy to see with the naked eye, although the nebula itself needs filters.

image.alt: The bright blue star 13 Scorpii inside a large round blue glow.
image.caption: Digitized Sky Survey 2 · STScI/NASA, colored by CDS · visible-light survey composite
image.credit: Digitized Sky Survey 2 (STScI/NASA; Palomar Observatory and UK Schmidt Telescope), colored by CDS. Archival photographic plates in blue and red light. Cutout centered on the nebula, north up, 600 × 600.

source.title: CDS and ESA: DSS colored survey

ic-426.name: IC 426

source.title: Magakian (2003): Merged catalogue of reflection nebulae

ic-426.introduction: is a reflection nebula about 1,370 light-years away in Orion, about a degree north of Alnilam, lit by the star HD 37140.

image.alt: A pale grey-blue cloud with a dark edge among red and pink stars.
image.caption: T.A. Rector/University of Alaska Anchorage, H. Schweiker/WIYN and NOIRLab/NSF/AURA · visible light
image.credit: T.A. Rector/University of Alaska Anchorage, H. Schweiker/WIYN and NOIRLab/NSF/AURA. Visible light. Cropped, Resized to 600 × 603 and converted to AVIF; colors unchanged.

sections.title: A disputed lamp
sections.text: Mintaka, the westernmost star in Orion’s Belt, lies about a degree away and has also been named as the source of the nebula’s light. Its dust scatters blue starlight toward us, while the red light is absorbed.

lbn-472.name: LBN 472
lbn-472.introduction: is a reflection nebula about 1,320 light-years away in Cepheus, around 6 Cephei, a hot star with emission lines in its spectrum.

image.alt: A blue nebula around a bright star at upper right, with grey dust and a red arc at left.
image.caption: Alpha Zhang · visible light and hydrogen-alpha · 2026
image.credit: Alpha Zhang. Visible light and hydrogen-alpha, 2026. Resized to 600 × 400 and converted to AVIF; colors unchanged.

ngc-6726.name: NGC 6726/6727
ngc-6726.introduction: is a pair of merging blue reflection nebulae about 510 light-years away in Corona Australis, in one of the closest star-forming clouds to the Solar System. Its appearance has earned it the nickname of the Rampaging Baboon Nebula.

image.alt: Two blue reflection nebulae, the upper one larger, with a small bright nebula and black dust between them.
image.caption: ESO · Wide Field Imager, visible light · released 2010
image.credit: ESO. Wide Field Imager, visible light, released 2010. Resized to 600 × 585 and converted to AVIF; colors unchanged.

source.title: ESO: The R Coronae Australis region

sections.title: A stellar nursery next door
sections.text: Johann Schmidt first recorded the nebulae in 1865, along with nearby NGC 6729. They lie in the Corona Australis cloud, which holds about 7,000 times the Sun’s mass and is at its most active in the Coronet, a loose cluster of about 30 young stars. The dust blocks so much light that it dims stars behind it by up to 45 magnitudes.

ic-4812.name: IC 4812
ic-4812.introduction: is a blue reflection nebula about 510 light-years away in Corona Australis, lit by the close pair of stars HD 176269 and HD 176270. It lies south-west of NGC 6726 in the same star-forming cloud, one of the nearest to the Solar System.

image.alt: A soft blue nebula around a bright pair of stars, bordered by dark dust and reddish clouds.
image.caption: ESO · Wide Field Imager, visible light · released 2010
image.credit: ESO. Wide Field Imager, visible light, released 2010. Cropped, Resized to 600 × 565 and converted to AVIF; colors unchanged.

source.title: ESO: The R Coronae Australis region

toby-jug-nebula.name: Toby Jug Nebula
toby-jug-nebula.introduction: is a butterfly-shaped reflection nebula about 1,420 light-years away in Carina, made by the star inside it. Rare among reflection nebulae, it is built from dust expelled by V341 Carinae, a red giant at the end of its life. It is also known as IC 2220.

image.alt: A butterfly-shaped orange-white nebula around a bright red giant star.
image.caption: ESO · VLT, visible light · released 2013
image.credit: ESO. VLT, visible light, released 2013. Resized to 600 × 600 and converted to AVIF; colors unchanged.

sections.title: Named after a drinking mug
sections.text: British astronomers Paul Murdin, David Allen and David Malin named it after the Toby jug, an old English drinking vessel they remembered from their youth. Its arcing structure does look a little like a jug with a handle.

source.title: ESO: Toby Jug Nebula press release (eso1343)

sections.title: A giant only 50 million years old
sections.text: V341 Carinae has five times the mass of the Sun, yet it is already a red giant at about 50 million years old, because massive stars burn through their fuel fast. The Sun will swell the same way, billions of years from now.

source.title: ESO: Toby Jug Nebula press release (eso1343)

sections.title: Shaped like a magnet’s field
sections.text: The nebula’s filaments resemble the field of a magnetic dipole, centered on the star. Two separate bubble-like structures show that the star shed mass at least twice. A very large closed loop has been tentatively interpreted as a giant prominence rising from the star.

vdbh-7.name: vdBH 7

source.title: Van den Bergh & Herbst (1975): Catalogue of southern stars embedded in nebulosity

vdbh-7.introduction: is a faint blue reflection nebula about 1,890 light-years away in Puppis, around the hot star HD 68982. It comes from the southern catalog of Sidney van den Bergh and Gretchen Herbst, the counterpart to van den Bergh’s northern list.

image.alt: A bright blue-white star inside a faint round blue glow, among scattered stars.
image.caption: Digitized Sky Survey 2 · STScI/NASA, colored by CDS · visible-light survey composite
image.credit: Digitized Sky Survey 2 (STScI/NASA; Palomar Observatory and UK Schmidt Telescope), colored by CDS. Archival photographic plates in blue and red light. Cutout centered on the nebula, north up, 600 × 600.

source.title: CDS and ESA: DSS colored survey

sh-2-64.name: W40
sh-2-64.introduction: is one of the closest sites of massive star formation, about 1,640 light-years away in Serpens, where gas surrounds a cluster of several hundred newborn stars. Dark clouds in the Aquila Rift hide it so well that it looks unimpressive in visible light. It is also known as Westerhout 40 and Sh 2-64.

image.alt: A pink, hourglass-shaped double bubble of glowing gas around a bright star cluster, in infrared light.
image.caption: NASA/JPL-Caltech · Spitzer, infrared · released 2019
image.credit: NASA/JPL-Caltech. Spitzer, infrared, released 2019. Resized to 600 × 391 and converted to AVIF; colors unchanged.

source.title: Wikimedia Commons: The Spitzer view of W40

sections.title: An hourglass blown by young stars
sections.text: Radiation and winds from the cluster have blown a two-lobed bubble in the surrounding cloud, giving the glowing gas an hourglass shape. A late O-type star and three early B-type stars do most of the ionizing. Stars at the center of the cluster are about 0.8 million years old, and those at its edge about 1.5 million.

sections.title: Where the filaments were noticed
sections.text: ESA’s Herschel Space Observatory first noted the striking prevalence of filaments in star-forming clouds in this region. These threads of gas contain dense cores, many of which are likely to collapse and form stars.

sh-2-126.name: Sh 2-126
sh-2-126.introduction: is a large, faint glow of hydrogen spanning nearly 3 degrees of Lacerta, about 1,490 light-years away. It is ionized mainly by 10 Lacertae, a hot young star of the Lacerta OB1 association. It is also known as the Great Lacerta Nebula or the Star Funnel Nebula.

image.alt: A yellow funnel of lit dust around bright stars, in a red glow of hydrogen.
image.caption: T.A. Rector (University of Alaska Anchorage) and H. Schweiker (WIYN and NOIRLab/NSF/AURA) · visible light and hydrogen-alpha
image.credit: T.A. Rector (University of Alaska Anchorage) and H. Schweiker (WIYN and NOIRLab/NSF/AURA). Visible light and hydrogen-alpha. Resized to 600 × 598 and converted to AVIF; colors unchanged.

sections.title: The star that set a standard
sections.text: 10 Lacertae was one of the first O-type stars chosen as an anchor point for the MKK spectral classification, and it still represents the class O9V. In 2018 it held the record for the smallest angular diameter measured by the CHARA array, at just 0.11 milliarcseconds.

sections.title: A funnel of lit dust
sections.text: Inside the red glow lies the feature behind the nickname: a funnel of dark dust that looks yellow because bright stars nearby are lighting it.

sh-2-174.name: Sh 2-174
sh-2-174.introduction: is a faint cloud about 950 light-years away in Cepheus, one of the northernmost objects in the Sharpless catalog. It has a long-running identity problem: it may be an ancient planetary nebula, or simply interstellar gas lit by a passing white dwarf. It is also known as the Valentine Rose Nebula.

image.alt: A red cloud with a sharp blue edge at right and a very blue white dwarf inside that edge.
image.caption: T.A. Rector (University of Alaska Anchorage) and H. Schweiker (WIYN and NOIRLab/NSF/AURA) · visible light and narrowband filters · released 2013
image.credit: T.A. Rector (University of Alaska Anchorage) and H. Schweiker (WIYN and NOIRLab/NSF/AURA). Visible light and narrowband filters, released 2013. Resized to 600 × 698 and converted to AVIF; colors unchanged.

sections.title: A star outside its own nebula
sections.text: The white dwarf GD 561 was identified in 1970, and in 1993 its spectrum was found to resemble those of the central stars of known planetary nebulae. In 1994, astronomers confirmed its link with the nebula, but found the star lying outside the cloud.

sections.title: A planetary-nebula mimic
sections.text: Frew and Parker argued in 2010 that this gas was never shed by the star. In their view, it is interstellar gas ionized by the white dwarf as it passes through.

source.title: Frew & Parker (2010): Planetary nebulae: observational properties, mimics and diagnostics

iswe-1.name: IsWe 1

source.title: Weidmann et al. (2020): Catalogue of central stars of planetary nebulae, expanded edition

iswe-1.introduction: is a large, faint planetary nebula about 1,390 light-years away in Perseus. Its central star is of the rare PG 1159 type, a hot, hydrogen-poor star on its way to becoming a white dwarf.

lotr-5.name: LoTr 5
lotr-5.introduction: is a large, faint planetary nebula about 1,480 light-years away in Coma Berenices, which in 2018 had the highest galactic latitude of any known planetary nebula, only 1.5 degrees from the galactic north pole. A. J. Longmore and S. B. Tritton discovered it in 1980 on photographic plates from the UK Schmidt Telescope.

image.alt: A small round blue shell with a dark hole beside its bright central star.
image.caption: Hunter Outten · visible light and oxygen filter · 2026
image.credit: Hunter Outten. Visible light and oxygen filter, 2026. Resized to 600 × 393 and converted to AVIF; colors unchanged.

sections.title: A peanut seen end-on
sections.text: Models show two round lobes in the shape of a peanut, with the long axis tilted only 17 degrees from our line of sight. The two lobes therefore overlap, which makes the bipolar nebula look nearly round. A binary at its center probably played a part in shaping it.

sections.title: An odd couple at the center
sections.text: At the heart are an evolved G-type star, IN Comae Berenices, and one of the hottest stars known, at about 150,000 K. They take 7.36 years to orbit each other, one of the longest periods known in a planetary nebula. The G-type star is rich in barium and covered with starspots that cause it to vary.

mwp-1.name: MWP 1
mwp-1.introduction: is the Methuselah Nebula, an unusually large and old planetary nebula about 1,640 light-years away in Cygnus. Its central star, RX J2117.1+3412, is one of the hottest stars known, at about 150,000 K, so hot that it shines in X-rays.

image.alt: Blue filamentary arcs on both sides of a bright orange and pink bipolar core.
image.caption: T.A. Rector (University of Alaska Anchorage) and H. Schweiker (WIYN and NOIRLab/NSF/AURA) · oxygen and hydrogen-alpha filters

sections.title: A star that lit the way to its nebula
sections.text: Alain Maury first noticed the nebula in 1987 at the Palomar Schmidt telescope. In 1992, Motch, Werner and Pakull identified the X-ray source, and in the same year another team found the large nebula around it. That discovery proved that this star is a PG 1159 star, now pulsing every 600–1,000 seconds.

sections.title: Filaments and a faint S
sections.text: A bright inner region is surrounded by a bipolar structure of filaments and arcs, with a very faint S-shaped outer glow. At an expansion speed of 20 km/s, it has been growing for around 100,000 years, which fits the name.

tk-1.name: TK 1

source.title: Orbits of nearby planetary nebulae and their interaction with the interstellar medium (2011)

tk-1.introduction: is a very large, very faint planetary nebula about 1,800 light-years away in Cancer, spanning more than the width of the full Moon. Physically it is about 15 light-years across, bigger even than Sh 2-216.

sections.title: Found by looking around a white dwarf
sections.text: Tweedy and Kwitter found this nebula in 1994 during a search around the hot, hydrogen-rich white dwarf Ton 320. Its very low density shows that it has reached a late stage. The star has moved away from the center of the nebula, and bright filaments in the south-east reveal where the shell is colliding with interstellar gas.

wede-1.name: WeDe 1

source.title: Napiwotzki (1999): Spectroscopic investigation of old planetaries IV

wede-1.introduction: is a large, faint, old planetary nebula about 1,890 light-years away in Orion. Its central star is distinctly hotter and more massive than is typical, at around 141,000 K and 0.68 solar masses.
